content.content:
The content-custody read is one crossing. A single spawned `jj log` invocation, whose template carries the diff summary, returns every change the substrate reports, each paired with the paths that change touched: a change never arrives without its paths, and a path never arrives without the change that touched it. Nothing narrows the set at this boundary. No ownership test and no path filter is applied to what the listing gives, because narrowing to the paths the nodes claim would presuppose the answer the pass is asking for; and the paths are the ones the summary prints for that change, not a changed set recomputed from the tree. The summary is the form the working-copy read already uses for one revision (vkowzusm), read here for each change the listing names, and a rename's two sides are the two paths the summary names for it.

What it does not read is content. No path's bytes cross this boundary: the crossing reports which paths a change touched and never what those paths hold, so an answer drawn from it can be about attribution and cannot be about comparison. It reads nothing about ownership, claims or verdicts either — the owning set, the rule that confronts it with what history recorded, and what a caller prints are settled elsewhere — and it neither replaces nor widens the working-copy read (vkowzusm), which stays what it is.

The fallbacks stay fallbacks. A change the set read cannot serve is read on its own, and a set read that cannot run is replaced by reading the changes one at a time: the per-object and whole-set forms the bound permits, and neither is the healthy path, which is one crossing for the whole set. The degraded forms exist so that a change is not silently dropped when the set read fails, not so that they can become the read's ordinary work. What a change or path no form could serve means is left where it is settled: a change the check cannot attribute is not thereby clean (xotxspwp).
content.rationale:
One crossing because the cost of this layer is process spawning (rkoktpwt): a read per change would make the spawn count grow with the number of changes, and a second crossing to collect the paths would double the one the listing already made. So the summary rides the listing that names the changes — the pairing is a property of the format the crossing asks for, not of joining two answers that could disagree about which change a path belongs to — and the paths this layer speaks about are the summary's own, the same form the working-copy read takes for one revision (vkowzusm). The crossing itself is a spawned process like every other interaction with the substrate (xmxpvqzs); how its failures are carried is that decision's, not this one's.

It refuses a per-change read as the shape and a second read for the paths, since either turns the healthy path into the loop the bound forbids. It refuses any content read at this boundary, because saying which paths a change touched needs no bytes of them, and reading them would put a comparison at a seam that should only report attribution, widening the width vkowzusm fixes. It refuses to filter the set, since a crossing returning only the changes that own nodes, or only the paths the documents list, would have decided the question the pass exists to ask. And it takes the ownership rule as given rather than restating, loosening or pre-empting it (xotxspwp).

What it leaves to its dependants: which module carries the crossing and how the crate spells it; what the pass prints for a disagreement, in what order and with what status; and what a caller makes of a fallback that failed. None of those changes what the crossing returns — the changes, each with the paths it touched, and no content.
